reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in establishing a consistent and fair ranking mechanism for incomplete tournaments where not all teams face each other. The paper introduces a family of scoring methods grounded in the principle of points-per-game, which allows for flexible point assignments based on outcomes. These methods satisfy fairness axioms such as anonymity and consistency, ensuring that no arbitrary labeling affects the final ranking. Efficiency is measured by how closely observed rankings approximate those from a hypothetical complete tournament. However, high-efficiency methods often exhibit unfairness due to inherent biases in partial data. The win percentage method serves as a limiting case within this family, offering simplicity but limited adaptability. The framework enables Bayesian inference of team strength and supports conformal prediction techniques for uncertainty quantification. Dualities emerge between efficiency and fairness—optimizing one often compromises the other. Failure modes include overfitting to small sample sizes and misalignment with true competitive strength when opponents vary widely in quality. The mathematical structure supports recursive state updates in GSE’s dynamic ranking engine, enabling real-time adaptation to new match results.
